H_hierarchical.evidence: The controller separates manual and auto modes, and auto mode contains waiting, direction selection, movement, slow-down, stop, and level-confirmation steps.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Auto direction is guarded by arithmetic over levels: destination level minus source/current level; negative selects up, positive selects down.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Transitions compute counters and direction, command VFD forward/reverse/slow/stop/reset, set tower lamps, and raise error/alarm outputs.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: Safety sensors cut and stop lift operation, over-travel alarms the system, and any alarm sends the whole lift into emergency requiring acknowledgement.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Sensor semantics are in Section 2, VFD commands in Section 3, mode sequencing in Section 4, lamp behavior in Section 5, and emergency behavior in the conclusion.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as safety interlocks, inching, manual/maintenance mode, emergency case, and alarm acknowledgement imply control rules beyond explicit state labels.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Mode actions such as tower-lamp indications and emergency alarm handling are described narratively outside the main operational sequence.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The direction guard depends on the arithmetic expression destination level minus source/current level.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: Auto/manual modes have parent-mode behavior such as fixed slow manual speed and continuous tower-lamp indications in addition to internal movement steps.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The paper states that whenever an alarm occurs the whole lift goes into an emergency case requiring operator acknowledgement.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: Auto mode has a shallow default waiting-for-command behavior before internal travel steps, but no deep composite init chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The level-difference sign guard is arithmetic and useful for expression checking, but there are not three or more complex arithmetic-boolean guards.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Any alarm globally forces the lift into emergency, and mode-level continuous lamp behavior can be declared once rather than duplicated.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Error, alarm, and operator acknowledgement are abstract notification actions, while most other effects are concrete VFD or sensor I/O.

key_nl_quotes: Counter value = Command Level - Current Position level.
Whenever an alarm occurs whole lift goes into emergency case.
one_line_pitch: This lift controller is a strong stress test because arithmetic level guards, mode-local actions, cross-section action attribution, and global emergency behavior all interact in one compact PLC case.
rationale: The paper provides enough concrete operational detail to build an EFSM: manual and auto modes, level-difference direction logic, sensor-gated slow/stop behavior, VFD outputs, and confirmation/error branches. It directly targets baseline-weak regions because guards and actions are split across prose, figures, wiring, simulation, and conclusion sections. The global alarm-to-emergency rule and parent-mode lamp/speed behavior make it especially difficult for flat Umple-style extraction.
